subject: dym-ft
title: DYM.FT.------C.FO.ACT.
description: Second diagram on page 450, paired with INFO-DY × ALT-FT above. Where the first diagram structurally shows how sixties information-dynamics could not reach alternative-functionalism across the diagonals, this one structurally shows the same fragmentation at the level of *form* itself: DYM-FT (dynamic functionalism — what alternative form *does* in working motion) crossed with C-FO-ACT (central focused activism — what political activism *does* in working motion). DYM-FT sits on the left with the subject-arrow; SCI-DY (scientific dynamics) rises above as the subject's upward output, with IST-F (isolated focus) at the lower-left as the subject's downward output. INFO-DY hangs centrally below DYM-FT as the subject's working hub. C-FO-ACT is partner-center; METH (method) rises above it and CULT-SOLD (culture-soldered) sits between C-FO-ACT and the upper-right margin, with PART (participation) anchoring the upper-right and RT-ALGN (reality alignment) below PART, and DEF (definition) on the right margin as the partner's eastern output. MT-INFO (meta-information) hangs at the bottom-center as the bridging-axis bottom terminus. Structural argument: Cecil Taylor's remark the next page records — that the black political activists 'had practically no knowledge of who they were' — is exactly this crossing's failure. C-FO-ACT routes upward through METH and CULT-SOLD into PART and RT-ALGN — but PART terminates at DEF (definition) rather than crossing back into DYM-FT's SCI-DY. Meanwhile DYM-FT's INFO-DY routes downward into MT-INFO without ever reaching CULT-SOLD on the partner-axis. The activist 'who they were' lives in DYM-FT's SCI-DY — but the partner-axis terminates in DEF, leaving the activists with definitions of activism rather than the dynamic-functionalism that would supply the self-knowledge Cecil names. The structural diagonals that would let SCI-DY meet CULT-SOLD are exactly what sixties fragmentation could not hold.
